subject: Post-demo: clarify hosting preference & staged PoC charter
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Nguyen <emily@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 May 2025 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: clarify hosting preference & staged PoC charter

Hi Emily — thanks again for taking the demo with the team today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we stay aligned on deployment fit (hosted API vs dedicated vs private VPC) and a pragmatic PoC approach.

Call highlights (short):
- Workload: low-latency conversational queries (~1–2k qps peak, many short prompts), batch embedding jobs overnight (~100k docs/day), HL7 ingestion from their ETL.
- Privacy: plan may involve PHI; security team flagged VPC and KMS as likely requirements.
- Latency & scale goals: p95 < 40ms, p99 target < 120ms for conversational inference; embeddings throughput ~100k/day in batch windows.
- Procurement window: you mentioned procurement review in Q3; pilot budget will need to be explicit if we hit dedicated/private.

Proposed staged PoC (to help choose deployment mode):
1) Hosted trial (2 weeks): our hosted API with dataset and eval prompts — validate model outputs, latency profile for typical queries, and integration patterns. Good low-friction start.
2) Dedicated trial (2–4 weeks): reserved capacity in your preferred region to test throughput under realistic concurrency and measure unit economics.
3) Private VPC pilot (timeboxed, only if PHI gating requires): customer-managed VPC + optional on-prem connector for audit and KMS control.

Success criteria (suggested; please edit):
- Functional: model quality F1 > baseline on 3 sample prompts and no blocking hallucination cases for top-10 intents.
- Performance: p95 < 40ms, p99 < 120ms for a 512-token context in hosted test; dedicated target: p99 < 80ms.
- Scale: sustained 2k concurrent users in dedicated test without >1% error rate.
- Security/compliance: pass initial vendor questionnaire items flagged as high risk (see attached list from your security team).

Ask from your side: can you confirm whether HealthGrid requires PHI handling for the pilot (yes/no) and which of the three stages you'd prefer us to run first? If you want to start with hosted, we can schedule a hosted-kickoff and share a mutual action plan (MAP) within 48 hours.

Proposed hosted kickoff window: Mon 2 June or Tue 3 June, 9–11am PT.

I attached the security Qs you shared during the call for visibility. We'll draft the MAP and cost notes based on your initial preference.

Thanks —
Sergio
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: HealthGrid_Security_Questions.pdf (from you)
From: Emily Nguyen <emily@healthgrid.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 May 2025 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: clarify hosting preference & staged PoC charter

Thanks Sergio — good recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- We do expect PHI in scope for the pilot (clinical notes + some identifiers). Our security team will insist on VPC/KMS for anything beyond exploratory testing.
- That said, procurement is slow; we'd prefer a low-friction hosted trial first to validate model fit before committing to dedicated/private. Cost will be the gating factor for dedicated.
- Our rough targets: p99 latency < 100ms (we can be flexible if that reduces cost), peak concurrency ~1.5k, embeddings batch ~100k/day overnight.

Can you provide an estimated delta in monthly cost between hosted vs dedicated for the expected footprint? Also please share what additional evidence you can provide for PHI handling and SOC2 scope so our security team can triage faster.

We can do the hosted kickoff the week of June 2 — Tue 3 June 10am PT works for our engineers.

Emily
Product Manager, HealthGrid
emily@healthgrid.com

Attachment: HealthGrid_Security_Questions.pdf
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 May 2025 13:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: clarify hosting preference & staged PoC charter

Emily — perfect, thanks for the clarity. Hosted-first + VPC-readiness if needed is a pragmatic path. Action plan (draft MAP) attached — I also pasted the short version below so everyone has a single view.

MAP (short):
- Week 0 (prep, by 29 May): exchange sample dataset, security questionnaire (you already sent), confirm retention rules and KMS needs. Owners: HealthGrid: Emily (data); Redwood: Monica (security packet).
- Week 1 (hosted trial, 2–3 June): run integration tests, gather latency telemetry, run embedding batch. Owners: HealthGrid eng: TBD; Redwood eng: Karthik (trial infra).
- Week 3 (dedicated trial window, optional): if hosted metrics meet quality but you want cost/throughput validation, spin up a dedicated pool for 2 weeks. Owners: Redwood infra: Marissa (provision & cost estimate).
- Decision point (end of PoC): choose Hosted/Dedicated/Private based on success criteria and procurement appetite.

Success criteria (finalizable):
- Quality: pass 3 representative prompt sets with <5% intent regression vs baseline.
- Latency: hosted p95 < 40ms, p99 < 100–120ms; dedicated p99 goal < 80ms.
- Scale & errors: <1% 5xx error rate at 1.5k concurrent baseline.
- Security: triage of high-risk items complete; for private path need KMS integration checklist and SOC2 evidence.

Costs: Marissa and I will put together a simple hosted vs dedicated delta chart (monthly run-rate estimate) after we lock on typical token volumes — we used 150M tokens/month for a similar account as a proxy. We'll share that by Mon 26 May.

Attachments: MAP_HealthGrid_v1.docx (draft mutual action plan)

Best,
Sergio
